scenes.title: Noah prepares the ark

art.alt: Noah applies dark pitch to a large wooden ark beside its visible side door; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 6:14–16, 22 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Wood, pitch, and the side door
intro.note: Genesis describes the ark's wood, pitch, window, side door, and three stories, then says Noah followed the command. The building scene reconstructs those details without claiming an exact hull design or location.

hotspots.title: Build with wood
hotspots.note: The command specifies gopher wood, rooms, and dimensions. The wood species and exact ark form cannot be established from this reconstruction.

hotspots.title: Pitch within and without
hotspots.note: Noah applies dark pitch to the wooden side. Genesis names pitch inside and outside; the tool and pot are reconstructed.

hotspots.title: A door in the side
hotspots.note: The visible opening illustrates the door placed in the ark's side. Genesis also describes a window and three stories.

scenes.title: The bow in the cloud

art.alt: A rainbow arches through clouds above Noah and a small group of living animals on renewed ground; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 9:12–17 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: A covenant sign after the flood
intro.note: The bow in the cloud is named as the covenant token for Noah and every living creature. The landscape and animal grouping are reconstructed; the image does not depict God speaking.

hotspots.title: The bow in the cloud
hotspots.note: God names the bow in the cloud as the token of the covenant between himself and the earth. The rainbow is the visible subject.

hotspots.title: Every living creature
hotspots.note: The covenant includes every living creature. The sheep and cattle represent living creatures; this animal grouping is illustrative.

scenes.title: Bricks for a city and tower

art.alt: Builders handle fired bricks and dark mortar beside an unfinished tall brick tower; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 11:3–4 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Building Babel
intro.note: Genesis names fired bricks and slime for mortar before the people propose their city and tower. This illustration represents the building project; it does not establish the tower's actual shape or height.

hotspots.title: Brick and mortar
hotspots.note: The builders make fired bricks and use slime for mortar. The visible reddish brick and dark mortar illustrate those materials.

hotspots.title: A city and tower
hotspots.note: The people propose a city and a tower to make themselves a name. Its stepped shape and scaffolding are reconstructed.

scenes.title: Abram departs with his household

art.alt: Abram and Sarai lead a modest household procession carrying possessions on pack animals; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 12:4–5 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Leaving Haran
intro.note: Abram departs with Sarai, Lot, their possessions, and the people with them. The procession and landscape illustrate departure without fixing a surveyed route or the appearance of Haran.

hotspots.title: Abram, Sarai, and Lot depart
hotspots.note: Abram leaves Haran with Sarai his wife and Lot his brother's son. The visible travelers illustrate the departure; their appearance is reconstructed.

hotspots.title: They take their possessions
hotspots.note: The household takes its gathered substance and people. The loaded pack animal represents those possessions without establishing an exact inventory or route.

scenes.title: Abram and Lot separate

art.alt: Abram and Lot speak beside a tent while a household and flocks prepare to depart toward a greener plain; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 13:8–12 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Room for two households
intro.note: Abram asks that there be no strife. Lot chooses the well-watered plain and they separate. The figures, tents, and land are a narrative reconstruction, not proof of precise directions or campsite locations.

hotspots.title: Let there be no strife
hotspots.note: Abram urges Lot to avoid strife and offers him the choice of land. The open-hand conversation illustrates this peaceful separation.

hotspots.title: Lot takes his household toward the plain
hotspots.note: Lot chooses the well-watered plain, journeys east, and pitches his tent toward Sodom. The tent and flock identify a moving household; their screen position is not a geographic bearing.

scenes.title: Melchizedek brings bread and wine

art.alt: Melchizedek offers bread and a wine vessel to Abram, with a respectful blessing gesture; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 14:18–19 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: A blessing for Abram
intro.note: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, brings bread and wine and blesses Abram. The exchange, clothing, and vessels are reconstructed. The later tithe is not depicted in this selected scene.

hotspots.title: Melchizedek brings bread and wine
hotspots.note: The bread and wine vessel illustrate what Melchizedek brings forth as king of Salem and priest of the most high God.

hotspots.title: Melchizedek blesses Abram
hotspots.note: Melchizedek blesses Abram in the name of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth. The raised hand represents his spoken blessing.

scenes.title: Abram looks toward the stars

art.alt: Abram stands outside a tent looking upward at a star-filled night sky; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 15:5–6 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: So shall thy seed be
intro.note: Abram is told to look toward heaven and number the stars, then believes the LORD. This image shows Abram and the visible stars; faith and the spoken promise are conveyed by the passage, not by a visible divine figure.

hotspots.title: Abram looks toward heaven
hotspots.note: Abram is brought outside and told to look toward heaven. He believes the LORD; the visible man illustrates Abram's attention, while the text conveys his faith.

hotspots.title: Number the stars
hotspots.note: The stars illustrate the comparison given for Abram's seed. Their pattern is artistic and does not identify an exact ancient sky.

scenes.title: Hagar beside the wilderness fountain

art.alt: Hagar sits beside a clear wilderness spring with a water vessel, looking toward an unseen speaker; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 16:7–8, 13–14 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Seen in affliction
intro.note: The angel of the LORD finds Hagar by a fountain in the wilderness. Hagar speaks of the God who sees her, and the well is named Beer-lahai-roi. The messenger remains unseen in this illustration; the woman's appearance and the water source are reconstructed.

hotspots.title: Hagar is found in the wilderness
hotspots.note: The angel of the LORD finds Hagar by a fountain and asks where she has come from and where she is going. The illustration shows Hagar; the speaker remains unseen.

hotspots.title: The fountain and the named well
hotspots.note: Hagar speaks of the God who sees her, and the well is named Beer-lahai-roi. The visible water identifies this setting without claiming its exact geography or construction.

scenes.title: Lot escapes toward Zoar

art.alt: Lot approaches a small town entrance at sunrise while fire and smoke rise over distant cities; non-graphic artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 19:22–24 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Haste thee, escape thither
intro.note: Lot is urged to escape to Zoar and enters as the sun rises; the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah follows. This reconstruction joins adjacent moments into one view. It shows no casualties and does not establish the cities' actual locations.

hotspots.title: Lot enters Zoar at sunrise
hotspots.note: Lot is urged to escape to Zoar and enters when the sun has risen. The visible man entering the gate represents Lot; the gate and companions' appearance are reconstructed.

hotspots.title: Fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah
hotspots.note: Genesis describes brimstone and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah. The distant burning cities illustrate this non-graphically; their location relative to Zoar is an editorial composition.

scenes.title: Sarah is restored to Abraham

art.alt: Sarah rejoins Abraham as Abimelech presents a bowl of silver with sheep and oxen nearby; artistic reconstruction

scenes.caption: Illustrated reconstruction · Genesis 20:14, 16 · Appearance and setting are illustrative

intro.title: Restoration and gifts
intro.note: Abimelech restores Sarah and gives Abraham sheep, oxen, servants, and silver. The image depicts the restoration and gifts without portraying people as saleable objects or adding a sexual encounter.

hotspots.title: Sarah is restored to Abraham
hotspots.note: Abimelech restores Sarah to Abraham. The visible couple illustrates her return; faces, clothing, and the setting are reconstructed.

hotspots.title: Sheep and oxen are given
hotspots.note: Sheep and oxen are among the gifts Abimelech gives Abraham. The visible animals represent those gifts; the attendants are shown with dignity.

hotspots.title: The gift of silver
hotspots.note: Abimelech tells Sarah of the silver he has given. The bowl represents silver pieces without claiming an exact ancient form or counting the thousand named in the verse.
